text:
jamie: Heads-up — after the kernel rollout in eu-west at ~03:10 UTC a subset of GPU nodes failed device-plugin registration, lots of pods stuck in ContainerCreating.
infra-oncall: Seeing many nodes flapping NotReady; kubelet logs show "nvidia: probe failed - kernel module mismatch" and device plugin health checks timing out.
devops-bot: [deploy] gpu-operator v1.8.0 started 03:09 UTC (auto-rollout).
sofia: Symptoms: pods requesting nvidia.com/gpu stay Pending or ContainerCreating, scheduler sometimes schedules CPU-only fallback jobs, batch pipeline retries exploding.
matt: Collected kubelet logs from gpu-eu-3 -> "failed to load nvidia driver: module version 525.x but kernel ABI 470.x expected". Driver pod is CrashLoopBackOff with oops in dmesg.
rika: Device plugin version on nodes is v0.11.1; operator rolled driver image to nvidia/driver:525. Older kernels in this region still require 470 series. Looks like operator + kernel + driver alignment issue.
jamie: Quick attempts: drained and reimaged 2 nodes to new kernel -> driver pod came up. Rolling operator back to v1.7.0 fixed registration for those nodes after reboot, but cluster-wide we still have mismatch.
sofia: Workarounds: cordon affected nodes and avoid scheduling GPU jobs there OR pin driver to 470 on nodes with older kernels. Both are manual and disruptive.
matt: Can we add a scheduler preference to prefer nodes labeled gpu.driver=525 for workloads that need the newer CUDA? This would reduce cross-region failures while we stabilize.
rika: We can add nodeAffinity/preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution for critical workloads; also propose annotating nodes with driver-version and kernel-abi so operator can be region-aware.
sam: Submitted a device-plugin patch that tolerates short driver-reload windows and parses driver-version annotations instead of assuming operator uniformity. Testing in staging now.
jamie: Immediate plan (tl;dr): 1) pause gpu-operator rollouts in all regions; 2) pin driver/operator pairs per region; 3) add node labels (gpu.driver=<ver>, gpu.kernel=<abi>); 4) run canary with 5 nodes/region and monitor.
infra-oncall: Note for runbook: cap concurrent drains to 5 nodes/region to avoid mass spot churn and retries — we've observed cost spikes and queue depth increases when >10 drains happen in parallel.
sofia: I'll own the canary orchestration and add the scheduler affinity for critical queues. Tagging @matt and @rika for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
matt: One oddball: saw NCCL errors on a training job ("ncclTopoGetUniqueId failed"). Could be downstream of driver mismatch?
rika: Yes, NCCL failures are usually secondary to missing kernel modules / driver registration; fix driver alignment first.
jamie: After canary proves green we'll resume operator rollouts but with region-aware driver pins and a short cooldown between batches. Will author an RCA + checklist in #eng-infra-docs once complete.
sofia: Also adding a monitoring rule: alert when device-plugin unregisters > 3 nodes in 10m and when driver pod restartCount > 5 in 5m.
jamie: Thanks all — keep posting short updates here if you hit edge cases or need reimages.
